precepts.text: Let neither man nor beast taste any thing, nor feed, nor drink water; that is the affliction of the soul, tasting nothing at all.
precepts.point: From even unto even shall ye celebrate your sabbath, the ninth day of the month at even. Even unto even is how days are numbered, one complete day of twenty-four hours, not sunrise to sunrise, for the evening and the morning were the first day.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
On the tenth day of this seventh month, the same month as the blowing of trumpets, is the day of atonement, and “ye shall afflict your souls.” What is afflicting the soul? Nineveh shows it: “Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water.”

No eating, no drinking, no tasting anything at all. That goes for gum, because you can taste gum, and even toothpaste: the last thing you do before the fast begins is brush your teeth before the sun goes down, and the first thing after it ends is brush them after the sun goes down. If you can taste it, keep it out of your mouth.

It is serious: “whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people”, and whoever does any work that day, “the same soul will I destroy from among his people.”

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
Nineveh proclaimed a fast “by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.” Man and beast covered in sackcloth, crying mightily unto God and turning from evil.

Eliphaz claims Job's suffering proves Job was sinning, that snares are round about him and sudden fear troubles him because he stripped the naked and withheld bread from the hungry. But the Lord was only trying him. Nineveh shows what a people do when they are truly in sin: they turn from their evil way. The truth is the opposite of what Eliphaz says: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

precepts.text: Who can tell if God will turn and repent? No man can tell you the Most High will not forgive you when you change.
precepts.point: The truth is the opposite: when Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?” No man can tell you the Most High will not forgive you when you change. Nineveh did not know whether God would turn, but they turned from their evil way anyway, and left it to him.

Eliphaz has it backwards: he claims Job's suffering proves Job was sinning, and that therefore snares are round about him and sudden fear troubles him. But the Lord was only trying him. When Job had his riches he dealt righteously, helped people, taught people, and was looked up to like an elder in the city. No man can tell what the Most High will do with a man, and no man could tell Job he was under fierce anger for sin he did not commit.

points: The word of the Lord came unto Jonah the second time, saying, Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee.

note.label: Jonah 3: The Preaching That Turned Nineveh

points: Jonah arose and went unto Nineveh according to the word of the Lord; and he cried, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.

note.label: Jonah 3: The Preaching That Turned Nineveh

points: The people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.

The king arose from his throne, laid his robe from him, covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes, and made the decree that neither man nor beast taste anything, but be covered with sackcloth and cry mightily unto God.
Let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil that he had said that he would do unto them, and he did it not.
